summary: Active in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, John Claude White studied at Rugby School (1868) and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876). In 1876, he served as an Assistant Engineer for the Bengal Public Works Department.

John Clifford Holt works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, he held professorships at Bowdoin College (~1978–2018), Calgary (2006), and Chicago (attested 2026).

Working in linguistics and Indology, John Collinson Nesfield studied at Highgate School and Merton College. He taught at Highgate (1859–1864), Presidency University (~1867–1872), and Krishnagar Government College (~1872–1874), later becoming principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1878).

Religious studies scholar John Corrigan earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1975–1982). His career includes positions at the University of Virginia (~1982–1987), Arizona State University (~1987–2001), and Florida State University, where he chaired the Religion Department (~2001).

John Crawfurd worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803), served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808), and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
John Cripps Pembrey was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Oriental Reader at Clarendon Press, with his affiliation attested in 1904 and 1916.

John D. Dunne works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. His appointments include Emory University (~2005–2016) and a Distinguished Chair at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

John D. Kelly is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He holds a career at the University of Chicago (attested 2007, 2026), where he serves as Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and Social Sciences.

John D. Smith is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) before joining the University of Cambridge as University Lecturer (1984) and Professor (2001–2007).

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Rutgers and trained under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi, whom he succeeded. He taught at Naropa University (1974) and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009).
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under teachers Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman (attested 2002).

A scholar of sinology and linguistics, John DeFrancis studied at Yale University (~1937–1940) and Columbia University (~1940–1948). He held academic posts at Seton Hall University (~1961–1966) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1976).

Philosopher John Dewey studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1884–1894), University of Minnesota (~1888–1889), University of Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

Indologist and linguist John Dowson studied under Edwin Norris. He tutored at the East India Company College (~1855–1858) and served as Professor of Hindustani at University College London and the Staff College, Camberley (1855–1877).

John E. Cort is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed degrees at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–1974) and Harvard University (~1979–1984), and he has served as a Professor at Denison University since ~1993.

John F. Richards specialized in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of New Hampshire (~1957–1961) and UC Berkeley (~1961–1970), later holding faculty positions at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1977) and Duke University (~1977–2007).

Indologist and epigraphist John Faithfull Fleet studied at University College London (~1865–1867). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897) and Bombay Civil Service (~1867–1897), and was Epigraphist for the Government of India (1883–1886).
John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from ~1876 to 1903 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from ~1891 to 1903.
John Fraser studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1903–1906). He later held academic appointments at the University of Aberdeen (~1908–1921) and the University of Oxford (~1921–1945).

Indology and religious studies scholar John George Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford (~1884–1888) and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He was a Calcutta High Court Judge (~1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (~1923–1930).
